standard_prerequisites.name: The determinant module det_kappa(M) of a finite length module over a local ring, with admissible sequences and the three admissible relations
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, chow.tex, Section 'Periodic complexes' and the definitions of admissible sequences and of det_kappa preceding this lemma (the statement's phrase 'with notations as above' refers to them)
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the notion of admissible sequence, the three relations (vanishing when the sequence does not generate M, scaling by a unit and moving an element that is killed by m), and the fact that det_kappa(M) is generated by the symbols of admissible sequences; the replacement argument itself is carried out in the counted span.

core_obligations: Fix an admissible sequence (f_1, ..., f_l) of M with length_R(<f_1, ..., f_i>) = i for i = 1, ..., l, which exists exactly because M has finite length l, and reduce the claim to showing that every element of det_kappa(M) is a kappa-multiple of the single symbol [f_1, ..., f_l] (proof lines 15766-15773).

Show that an arbitrary admissible sequence (e_1, ..., e_l) with <e_1, ..., e_l> != M has vanishing symbol: some e_i lies in <e_1, ..., e_{i-1}>, and the first admissible relation forces [e_1, ..., e_l] = 0 (proof lines 15779-15784).

For an admissible sequence generating M, locate the smallest i with f_1 in <e_1, ..., e_i>, write e_i = lambda f_1 + x with lambda a unit and x in <e_1, ..., e_{i-1}>, use the second admissible relation to replace e_i by f_1, and then use m f_1 = 0 and the third admissible relation i-1 times to obtain [e_1, ..., e_l] = (-1)^{i-1} lambda-bar [f_1, e_1, ..., e_{i-1}, e_{i+1}, ..., e_l], and iterate this step inductively to convert the symbol into a scalar multiple of [f_1, ..., f_l] (proof lines 15785-15818).
proof_roadmap: Choose an admissible sequence (f_1, ..., f_l) whose initial segments have length i and reduce to producing [f_1, ..., f_l] as a generator (proof lines 15766-15773).
Dispose of the non-generating case with the first admissible relation (proof lines 15779-15784).
Run the replacement induction, moving f_1 to the front with the second and third admissible relations and tracking the sign and the unit, then repeat for f_2, ..., f_l (proof lines 15785-15818).
difficulty_reason: The statement is short but it is not self-contained: it says 'with notations as above' and asserts that dim_kappa(det_kappa(M)) <= 1 for a finite length module M over a local ring (R, m, kappa), where det_kappa is the determinant module built out of admissible sequences of M modulo the three admissible relations (statement lines 15760-15763). The proof cannot be a formal manipulation of the definition: it must pick an admissible sequence f_1,...,f_l with length_R(<f_1,...,f_i>) = i, then show that an arbitrary admissible sequence e_1,...,e_l either has vanishing symbol [e_1,...,e_l] = 0 (when it does not generate M) or can be transformed into a scalar multiple of the chosen symbol by repeatedly locating the smallest index with f_1 in <e_1,...,e_i>, writing e_i = lambda f_1 + x with lambda a unit, and applying the second and third admissible relations i-1 times to move f_1 to the front, followed by an induction on j (proof lines 15766-15818). The order of the admissible sequences, the unit, and the sign (-1)^{i-1} are exactly the content of the argument, so the claim is H2.
